title: Canonical derived scalar and pullback isomorphism
statement:
Let $A,B$ be commutative rings in the coefficient universe, $\varphi:A\to B$ a unital ring homomorphism, and $f:Z\to W$ any morphism of schemes. In the ordinary unbounded small-etale derived module categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], write $S_T=-\otimes_A^LB$ for canonical derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and $L f_R^*$ for the canonical derived geometric inverse image [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. Define $\operatorname{scalarPullbackIso}(\varphi,f)$ to be the unique natural isomorphism
$$c_f:Lf_B^*S_W\xrightarrow{\sim}S_ZLf_A^*$$
normalized by the ordinary scalar/pullback comparison on K-flat representatives [def-pc-kflat-complex], [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. More explicitly, let $F_T$ be ordinary scalar extension, $r_P:S_T\mathsf Q_AP\to\mathsf Q_BF_TP$ its representative counit, $g_{R,P}:Lf_R^*\mathsf Q_RP\to\mathsf Q_R(f_R^*P)$ the geometric representative counit, and $a_P:f_B^*F_WP\cong F_Zf_A^*P$ the termwise ordinary scalar/pullback isomorphism, adjunction-conjugate to the sectionwise restriction/direct-image comparison [lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons]. The defining normalization, for every K-flat cochain complex $P$ on $W$ with $A$-coefficients, is
$$c_{f,\mathsf Q_AP};S_Z(g_{A,P});r_{f_A^*P}=Lf_B^*(r_P);g_{B,F_WP};\mathsf Q_B(a_P).$$
Semicolons mean first the left arrow then the right arrow. The chosen isomorphism is the unique witness of this normalization; no flatness, boundedness, properness or invertibility-of-direct-image comparison hypothesis is added.

proof.text: Construct the normalized natural isomorphism by the existence theorem, and use the independently proved uniqueness theorem to show that this witness is unique. The chosen comparison definition remains the unique normalized witness.

lean.statement:
def scalarPullbackIso
    {A B : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    (φ : A →+* B) {Z W : Scheme.{u}} (f : Z ⟶ W) :
    scalarExtension φ W ⋙ L(upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B) f) ≅
      L(upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f) ⋙ scalarExtension φ Z
